Representative values for banded categories

Source: R/bands.R
bandvals.Rd

Gives each band a single number that a calculation can use (a mean, a concentration index, a regression), under a rule you choose. For closed bands the rule places the value at the midpoint, the lower or upper bound, or the geometric mean of the bounds. An open band ("50+", “under 18”) has no midpoint, so its missing bound is filled from an explicit assumption, and the rows that rest on that assumption are flagged in the result instead of being absorbed into it.

Usage

bandvals(
  bands,
  rule = c("midpoint", "lower", "upper", "geometric"),
  openupcap = NULL,
  openupfac = 2,
  openloflr = NULL
)

Arguments

bands

A data frame from prsbands, or a character vector of labels to parse with its defaults.

rule

Character, one of "midpoint" (the default), "lower", "upper" or "geometric". The geometric mean suits quantities whose distribution inside a band is closer to log-uniform than uniform, which is usual for counts and durations.

openupcap

Number or NULL (the default). The upper bound assumed for every open top band, in the units of the labels.

openupfac

Number, default 2. When no cap is given, the open top band's upper bound is its lower bound times this factor (so “Greater than 10” becomes 11 to 22).

openloflr

Number or NULL (the default). The lower bound assumed for an open bottom band (“under 18”). NULL uses 0, or the band's own upper bound when that is below 0. A floor above a band's upper bound is refused.

Value

The band table with two added columns: value (numeric, the representative value) and assumed (logical, TRUE for the open bands whose value rests on the cap or floor).

Details

For a band with bounds \([l, u]\) the value is \((l + u)/2\) ("midpoint"), \(l\) ("lower"), \(u\) ("upper") or \(\sqrt{l u}\) ("geometric"; when \(l \le 0\) the arithmetic midpoint is used instead, because the geometric mean is undefined there). The "lower" and "upper" rules bracket any value that could come from the bands.

An open upper band gets \(u =\) openupcap if given, else \(u = l \times\) openupfac. An open lower band gets \(l =\) openloflr if given, else \(\min(0, u)\). A cap below the band's lower bound, or a floor above its upper bound, is an error, because the value would lie outside the band. Unparsed bands give NA.

Use bandsens to see how much a result moves with the cap, and expbands to turn the values into one value per unit.

See also

prsbands, bandsens, expbands

Examples

b <- prsbands(c("1", "2 to 5", "6 to 10", "Greater than 10"))
bandvals(b)
#>             label lower upper openlo openup value assumed
#> 1               1     1     1  FALSE  FALSE   1.0   FALSE
#> 2          2 to 5     2     5  FALSE  FALSE   3.5   FALSE
#> 3         6 to 10     6    10  FALSE  FALSE   8.0   FALSE
#> 4 Greater than 10    11    NA  FALSE   TRUE  16.5    TRUE

# The lower and upper rules bracket the truth.
bandvals(b, rule = "lower")$value
#> [1]  1  2  6 11
bandvals(b, rule = "upper", openupcap = 40)$value
#> [1]  1  5 10 40

# geometric placement, and an explicit floor for an open bottom band
bandvals(b, rule = "geometric", openupcap = 40)$value
#> [1]  1.000000  3.162278  7.745967 20.976177
bandvals(c("under 5", "5 to 9", "10+"), openloflr = 1)
#>     label lower upper openlo openup value assumed
#> 1 under 5    NA     4   TRUE  FALSE   2.5    TRUE
#> 2  5 to 9     5     9  FALSE  FALSE   7.0   FALSE
#> 3     10+    10    NA  FALSE   TRUE  15.0    TRUE

# a cap inside the open band is refused
try(bandvals(b, openupcap = 5))
#> Error : the open-band cap (5) lies below the band's own lower bound (11); a midpoint there would be below every value in the band
